highlight.text: Here, Hiroshige devoted nearly half the composition to the night sky glittering with fireworks.

work.text: The Ryōgoku Bridge, a repeated subject of Hiroshige’s prints, spanned the Sumida River connecting bustling Edo (present-day Tokyo) neighborhoods.

source.author: Cleveland Museum of Art
source.title: Fireworks at Ryōgoku, from the series One Hundred Views of Famous Places in Edo

moment.text: Restaurants and other businesses along the riverbank frequently sponsored these dazzling displays during the 1850s.

source.author: Cleveland Museum of Art
source.title: Fireworks at Ryōgoku, from the series One Hundred Views of Famous Places in Edo

matters.text: The pyrotechnics drew large crowds, who gathered atop the bridge, along the shore, in teashops, and on rented pleasure boats to enjoy the show.
